source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Horizontal Lines: Swing Points and Other Key Price Levels

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; ma = ema(close, maLength); atr(n) is the n-bar average true range; swingHigh(k)/swingLow(k) = k-th most recent confirmed pivot

candidates.name: SwingPivot
candidates.quote: you will find that horizontal lines across swing highs and lows often serve as barriers that result in failed breakouts and then reversals.
candidates.description: Primitive: a swing low is a bar whose low is below the lows of the pivotStrength bars on each side; a swing high is the mirror. Confirmed pivotStrength bars after the pivot bar.
candidates.pseudocode: isSwingLow(i) = low[i] < lowest(low, pivotStrength) over bars i+1..i+pivotStrength && low[i] < lowest(low, pivotStrength) over bars i-pivotStrength..i-1; swingLow(1) = most recent i >= pivotStrength with isSwingLow(i)

complexity.reason: swing-pivot detection with a confirmation lag

candidates.name: FailedSwingExtremeBreakoutReversal
candidates.quote: Expect swing high breakouts to fail and form higher high reversal setups, and swing low breakouts to fail and form lower low reversal setups.
candidates.description: Long form (mirror of the book's short): the bar's low breaks below the most recent confirmed swing low but the bar closes back above that swing low; buy at the next open.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: needs a confirmed swing-low pivot at variable distance

notes: Same family as Chapter 10's FailedTestOfPriorSwingExtreme and Chapter 15's FailedChannelBreakoutReentry, applied here to a plain horizontal swing level rather than a projected trend/channel line.

candidates.name: SecondMoreExtremeReversalIsStronger
candidates.quote: Sometimes the failure fails, which is a breakout pullback setup, and the market makes a second more extreme higher high or lower low. A fade of a second higher high or lower low setup is even more likely to be successful, because they are second attempts to reverse the market.
candidates.description: Prefer T17-02 on the second occurrence of a failed swing-extreme breakout within lookback bars over the first.

complexity.reason: window count of a derived per-bar event

candidates.name: TradingRangeDayContext
candidates.quote: Most days are trading range days or have a lot of trading range activity. On these days you will find that horizontal lines across swing highs and lows often serve as barriers that result in failed breakouts and then reversals.
candidates.description: Gate T17-02/T17-03 on the day being a trading-range day rather than a trend day; on trend days horizontal lines should instead be used only for with-trend pullback entries (T17-05).

complexity.reason: 'trading range day' vs. 'trend day' is a discretionary daily-scale judgment with no single bar-level test given; a proxy (e.g., TrendingSwings false, or a Donchian-band-hug test) is a design decision

candidates.name: BreakoutLevelRetestBuy
candidates.quote: if there is a strong upside breakout of a trading range on a bull trend day, there might be a pullback to the area of breakout level after a few bars. If there is a bull reversal setup on the test, this is a good breakout pullback buy setup.
candidates.description: On a trend day, after an upside breakout of a trading range (close above its highest high), buy a pullback that retests the breakout level (within tolerance) with a bull reversal bar.
candidates.pseudocode: breakoutLevel = highest(high, rangeBars)[breakoutBar]; low[0] <= breakoutLevel + touchTolAtr * atr(atrLength) && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (0 - breakoutBar) <= maxWaitBars
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: the breakout level must be captured and held as persisted state from an earlier, variable-distance bar

candidates.name: FadeSwingExtremeRequiresPriorTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: On strong trend days, consider fading swing highs in bull trends and swing lows in bear trends only if there was first a good trend line break and a strong reversal bar.
candidates.description: On a trend day, only take the countertrend fade at a swing extreme against the trend if a trend line has already broken and the current bar is a strong reversal bar; otherwise skip it.
candidates.pseudocode: trendLineBrokenWithin(lookbackBars) && close[0] < open[0] && (open[0] - close[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && high[0] >= swingHigh(1) - touchTolAtr * atr(atrLength)
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop below the reversal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: needs the trend-line break state plus the swing-pivot reference

candidates.name: ScalpOnlyCountertrendOnMinimalMomentum
candidates.quote: since these are countertrend and there was only minimal countertrend momentum on the trend line breaks, these trades are not strong and should only be scalps.
candidates.description: When the trend-line break preceding a countertrend fade (T17-06) was itself small/slow, cap the trade's target to a scalp distance instead of a swing target.
candidates.pseudocode: (high[breakBar] - low[breakBar]) < minBreakAtrMultiple * atr(atrLength) -> exit at scalpTicks profit instead of a swing target

complexity.reason: a single ATR-relative size test on an already-identified break bar, then a fixed-tick target

candidates.name: TwentyGapBarPullbackSetup
candidates.quote: both days were strong trend days with one extreme near the open and then no moving average pullback for over two hours (20 gap bar pullback setups).
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a run of at least gapBarsThreshold consecutive bars all staying on one side of the EMA (never touching it), followed by the first bar to touch/cross back to it -- the '20 gap bars' pullback entry. Buy the first touch of the EMA after such a run.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceLastEmaTouch(maLength) >= gapBarsThreshold && low[0] <= ma && close[0] > ma
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the touch bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: needs an EMA plus a bars-since counter of how long price has avoided the average, in addition to the fixed-offset touch test

notes: The simpler one-bar-gap form (without the 20-bar run requirement) is MovingAverageGapBar, defined in the Chapter 07 and 15 mined files; this is the full run-length version referenced by name in Chapters 11, 16 and here.

candidates.name: MiddayCountertrendTrapWithTrendReentry
candidates.quote: They were after 11:30 a.m., when there is often a strong countertrend move that traps traders out of the trend and into the wrong direction. This sets up a reliable with-trend trade that usually results in a new extreme and often lasts into the close.
candidates.description: Intraday: after cutoffTime (late morning), a countertrend move that closes through the EMA (trapping with-trend traders out) but then resumes in the original trend direction is a high-quality with-trend re-entry.
candidates.pseudocode: time[0] >= cutoffTime && low[0] <= ma && close[0] > ma
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the touch bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: a time gate plus an EMA touch-and-hold test

rejected.quote: Bar 9 was the seventh point of an expanding triangle bottom (even though it was a double bottom with yesterday's low and not a lower low, close is close enough)
rejected.reason: single chart-specific labeling exercise using undefined multi-book pattern names (expanding triangle, wedge bull flag) with no new generalizable numeric test beyond primitives mined elsewhere.

rejected.quote: The two-sided forces continued to control the market and the market reversed up into the close, ending the day about where it began.
rejected.reason: narrative description of a single day's outcome, not a decidable rule.

chapter_summary: Chapter 17 mechanizes horizontal lines as the zero-slope special case of swing structure: on trading-range days, failed breakouts of swing highs/lows reverse, and a second, more extreme failure is a stronger signal than the first; on trend days the same levels should instead gate with-trend pullback retests of a breakout level or countertrend fades that require a prior trend-line break. It also fully defines the '20 gap bars' setup (a long run of bars never touching the EMA, then the first touch) that Chapters 11 and 16 reference by name but do not define, plus a related late-morning countertrend-trap re-entry. 'Trading range day' itself is graded research since Brooks gives no bar-level test to distinguish it from a trend day.
